  "markdown": "# Frequently Asked Questions

Answers to common questions received by the National Ocean Service on various topics

## Below are some of the questions we are asked most frequently, organized by theme. If you have a question that is not answered below, please [contact us](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/contact.html).

## Can I have permission to use your image or graphic? How do I credit NOAA?

#### **Can I use this image?**

Most of NOAA's information is in the ‘public domain’ and CANNOT be copyrighted. **Unless otherwise noted in the credit or caption of the item** of interest, you may use it without express permission. The one exception are our videos, as they often use third-party copyrighted footage. Video, in other words, will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. However, for most other content (e.g., our images, infographics, articles) you may use this material, but may not:

- Claim it as your own (i.e., claiming copyright for federal information);
- Use it in a manner that implies an endorsement or affiliation with the U.S. Government; or
- Modify the content or misrepresent the content, and then present it as official government material.

Credit should be given to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).


#### **Can I modify/crop infographics?**

You are welcome to link to our infographics (provide thumbnails that link back to the originals on our website), but we ask that people not modify/crop our infographics. The reason is that these are official NOAA products. If people modify them, we can no longer vouch for the accuracy of the material. Moreover, if something changes that would affect the content of those infographics (which often happens), we update our graphics on our website... but over time the accuracy of the infographics that are reproduced/shared externally would decline.


If you are uncertain about usage of particular product on our website, please [contact us](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/contact.html).

## How do I cite articles from this website?

#### How to cite National Ocean Service articles

_The following are examples of how to cite articles on this website. Citation formats will vary based on your chosen [style guide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Style_guide). Please note that we do not use author names for individual articles. When citing an article or resource from this website, use "NOAA" or spell out "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration" as the author._

**Web Page with Known Publication Date.** If a story has a listed publication or modification date on the page, cite as follows:

NOAA. What is eutrophication? National Ocean Service website, https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/eutrophication.html, 10/05/17.

**Web Page with Unknown Publication Date.** If a story does not have a listed publication or modification date on the page, cite as follows:

NOAA. Historical Maps and Charts audio podcast. National Ocean Service website, https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/podcast/july17/nop08-historical-maps-charts.html, accessed on 8/13/17.

## Can you help my scout troop with their merit badges?

The one program we had for this in Chesapeake, Virginia, is no longer active because the person running it on a volunteer basis has retired. We're not aware of any other NOAA programs of a similar nature.

## Can you help me research my student project or report? Can I interview a NOAA expert?

#### **Can you do my homework/research?**

We do not have the staff or resources to help you research your topic. For answers to common ocean-related questions, you can search the [National Ocean Service website](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/); our [Ocean Facts](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts) may be helpful as well. All content is in the public domain unless otherwise noted, and you may quote it in your schoolwork as long as you cite NOAA's National Ocean Service.

#### **Can I talk to an expert for my school project?**

NOAA does not have the staff or resources to provide informational interviews for school projects. We suggest contacting your public library or your county or university's [cooperative extension service](https://www.usda.gov/topics/rural/cooperative-research-and-extension-services) to find an expert on your topic.

#### **Sea level rise resources**

We do have a lot of resources online, however. Here are some that will help with your project:

- [Is sea level rising?](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/sealevel.html)
- [Sea Level Rise - NOS Education](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/sea-level-rise/welcome.html)
- [How is sea level rise related to climate change?](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/sealevelclimate.html)
- [Global vs. Local Sea Level](https://oceantoday.noaa.gov/globalvslocalsealevel/)

#### **Coral reef resources**

The following links may be helpful for your school project:

- [NOAA Coral Reef Conservation Program](http://coralreef.noaa.gov/)
- [NOS Infographics](http://oceanservice.noaa.gov/infographics/)
- [Coral reefs: Essential and threatened](http://www.noaa.gov/explainers/coral-reefs-essential-and-threatened)

#### **Ocean acidification resources**

Here are some resources that may be helpful to you related to ocean acidification:

- [What is Ocean Acidification? (NOS)](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/acidification.html)
- [What is Ocean Acidification? (PMEL)](https://www.pmel.noaa.gov/co2/story/What+is+Ocean+Acidification%3F)
- [Ocean acidification (NOAA)](https://www.noaa.gov/education/resource-collections/ocean-coasts/ocean-acidification)

#### **Noise pollution resources**

Here are a few resources that include webinars with questions and answers and other detailed infographics:

- [Understanding Sound in the Ocean](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/insight/understanding-sound-ocean)
- [Ocean Noise and Soundscape Projects](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/new-england-mid-atlantic/ocean-noise-and-soundscape-projects)
- [A Noisy Ocean: A Q&A with Dr. Leila Hatch](https://sanctuaries.noaa.gov/news/jun16/noisy-ocean.html)
- [Noise Sanctuary Sentinel Site Issue](https://sanctuaries.noaa.gov/science/sentinel-site-program/noise.html)

## What opportunities does NOAA offer for students, recent graduates, or volunteers?

#### **Scholarships, fellowships, internships**

While NOAA's opportunities are not managed through one centralized process, a great place to start is NOAA's [Student Opportunities](https://www.noaa.gov/education/opportunities/students) portal, which lists many open scholarships, internships, fellowships, and other programs throughout the agency — and you can easily filter this list by audience and opportunity type.

Many opportunities for students and recent graduates are also posted on [usajobs.gov](https://usajobs.gov/) as they become available, so it's worth checking back regularly.

#### **Volunteer**

NOAA offers many volunteering opportunities, including citizen science projects. Visit [NOAA's volunteering portal](https://www.noaa.gov/work-with-us/volunteer-opportunities-citizen-scientists) for more information.

#### **Job announcements**

NOAA job openings are posted on [usajobs.gov](https://usajobs.gov/) as they become available.

## Can you publicize or share my (non-.gov website, Facebook page, project) on your website?

As a U.S. federal agency, we cannot publicize, advocate for, or promote non-federal programs, businesses, nonprofits, or personal projects. We are also prohibited from directly or indirectly implying endorsement of non-government programs and activities, and are prohibited by law in activities that involve solicitation of funds or direct/indirect lobbying.


## Can you name a hurricane after me?

NOAA does not name tropical storms. There is a strict procedure established by the World Meteorological Organization. For Atlantic hurricanes, there is a list of male and female names that are used on a six-year rotation. The only time that there is a change is if a storm is so deadly or costly that the future use of its name on a different storm would be inappropriate. In the event that more than 21 named tropical cyclones occur in a season, any additional storms will take names from a backup list. Additional resources are available below.

- [How are hurricanes named?](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/storm-names.html)
- [Tropical cyclone naming: World Meteorological Organization](https://public.wmo.int/en/About-us/FAQs/faqs-tropical-cyclones/tropical-cyclone-naming)
- [World Meteorological Organization member nations](https://public.wmo.int/en/about-us/members)

## Can you provide feedback on or help me with my new business idea or invention?

By law, the U.S. Government is not able to accept unsolicited product recommendations or business proposals. This law guarantees that all companies are treated equally when competing for federal contracts. If you wish to respond to a federal contracting solicitation, you should visit the federal contracting portal here: https://sam.gov/. Not only will you find solicitations from NOAA, but from all federal agencies, which should save you some time.

We are also unable to provide feedback, advice, or help with unsolicited inventions, ideas, or plans.

#### **MORE INFORMATION**

National Ocean Service

[National Ocean Service Introduction (PDF)](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/introduction-nos.pdf)

* * *

[NOS Annual Accomplishments & Science Reports](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/reports.html)

[Explore the Breadth of NOS's Everyday Work and Mission](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/mission.html)

[About NOS Education](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/about.html)

[NOS Disaster Response Support](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/disaster-response/)

[NOS Environmental Compliance](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/environmental-compliance.html)

[NOS Grants](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/grants.html)

[NOS Organization Chart](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/nos_orgchart_1-22-2026.pdf)

[NOS Program Offices](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/programs/)

[NOS Roadmap](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/NOSRoadmap.pdf)

[NOS Science Seminars](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/about/science-seminars.html)

NATIONAL OCEANIC AND ATMOSPHERIC ADMINISTRATION

[NOAA.gov](https://www.noaa.gov/)

[NOAA Organizational Structure, Mission and Statutory Authority](https://www.performance.noaa.gov/)

[NOAA Office of Inclusion and Civil Rights](https://www.noaa.gov/organization/inclusion-and-civil-rights)

[NOAA No FEAR Act Information](https://www.noaa.gov/organization/inclusion-and-civil-rights/no-fear-act)

Department of Commerce

[U.S. Department of Commerce](https://www.commerce.gov/)

[DOC Strategic Plan and Annual Performance Plans](https://www.osec.doc.gov/bmi/budget/budgetsub_perf_strategicplans.htm)
